examples.en: The pants are so big that the waist is loose.
I must have lost weight, because my ring keeps feeling loose.

examples.ko: 신발이 헐렁거려서 오래 걸으면 발이 아파요.
examples.en: The shoes fit loosely, so my feet hurt when I walk for long.

examples.ko: 의자 다리가 헐렁거리고 삐걱거려서 앉기 무서워요.
examples.en: The chair leg is wobbly and creaky, so I'm scared to sit on it.

examples.ko: 헐렁거리는 옷을 입으면 편하지만 멋은 없어요.
examples.en: Loose clothes are comfortable, but they don't look stylish.

examples.ko: 이 바지는 허리가 헐렁거리지 않고 몸에 잘 맞아요.
examples.en: The waist of these pants isn't loose, and they fit well.

explain: '헐렁하다'는 옷이 몸에 비해 크다는 상태를 말하고, '헐렁거리다'는 헐거워서 흔들리는 느낌까지 있어요. 옷이 큰 것만 말할 때는 '헐렁하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 반대로 꼭 끼면 '꽉 끼다', 딱 맞으면 '딱 맞다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '헐렁하다' just describes clothes being too big, while '헐렁거리다' also gives the feeling of something loose and wobbling. To say only that clothes are big, '헐렁하다' sounds more natural. The opposites are '꽉 끼다' (fit too tight) and '딱 맞다' (fit just right).

examples.ko: 할아버지 댁 마당 옆에 큰 헛간이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a big shed next to the yard at my grandfather's house.
I put the farm tools in the shed.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 헛간 안에서 잠깐 쉬었어요.
examples.en: It rained, so we rested inside the barn for a while.

examples.ko: 헛간 문이 낡아서 잘 안 닫혀요.
examples.en: The shed door is old, so it doesn't close well.

examples.ko: 시골에서는 헛간에 장작이나 연장을 많이 보관해요.
examples.en: In the countryside, people often keep firewood or tools in the shed.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 헛간에서 고양이 새끼를 발견했어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I found a kitten in the barn.

explain: '창고'는 물건을 쌓아 두는 건물 전체를 넓게 말하고, '헛간'은 주로 시골집에서 농기구나 장작을 두는 허름한 건물에 써요. 도시에서는 거의 '창고'라고 해요.
explain_en: '창고' is a general word for any building used to store things, while '헛간' mostly means a simple shed on a farm or country house for tools and firewood. In the city people almost always say '창고'.

examples.en: Grandfather came into the room clearing his throat.
He felt awkward and only cleared his throat.
Before the presentation, I cleared my throat to get ready.
Suddenly I heard someone clearing their throat behind me.
When the children heard their father's throat-clearing, they went quiet.
It was hard to answer, so I got through it with a throat-clear.

explain: 감기 때문에 나오는 '기침'과 달리, '헛기침'은 아프지 않은데 일부러 하는 기침이에요. 어색할 때, 자기가 왔다는 걸 알릴 때, 주의를 끌 때 해요. 보통 '헛기침을 하다'라고 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '기침' (a cough from a cold), '헛기침' is done on purpose when you aren't sick. People do it when feeling awkward, to announce their presence, or to get attention. It is usually used as '헛기침을 하다'.

examples.en: Grandfather cleared his throat in front of the door and came in.

examples.ko: 말을 꺼내기 어려워서 몇 번 헛기침했어요.
examples.en: It was hard to bring it up, so I cleared my throat a few times.
When I'm embarrassed, I clear my throat without realizing it.
Why do you keep clearing your throat?
Someone in the back row cleared their throat on purpose.
He cleared his throat and changed the subject.

explain: '기침하다'는 몸이 아파서 하는 기침이고, '헛기침하다'는 신호를 보내거나 어색함을 감추려고 일부러 하는 기침이에요. 명사 '헛기침'과 같이 '헛기침을 하다'로도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: '기침하다' is coughing because of illness, while '헛기침하다' is a deliberate cough to send a signal or hide awkwardness. People also say '헛기침을 하다' with the noun.

examples.ko: 필요 없는 물건을 사서 헛돈만 썼어요.
examples.en: I bought things I didn't need and just wasted money.

examples.ko: 이 학원은 효과가 없어서 헛돈 쓴 기분이에요.
examples.en: This academy doesn't work, so I feel like I wasted my money.
I keep a household account book so I don't waste money.

examples.ko: 고쳐도 또 고장 나면 헛돈이 될까 봐 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried it will be wasted money if it breaks again after the repair.
I bought it because it was on sale and ended up throwing money away.

examples.ko: 헛돈 들이지 말고 꼭 필요한 것만 사세요.
examples.en: Don't waste money; buy only what you really need.

explain: '헛-'은 보람 없이 한다는 느낌을 더해요. '헛돈을 쓰다', '헛돈을 들이다', '헛돈을 날리다'처럼 자주 말해요. 비슷한 '돈 낭비'보다 아깝다는 감정이 더 강해요.
explain_en: The prefix '헛-' adds a sense of doing something in vain. It is often used as '헛돈을 쓰다', '헛돈을 들이다', or '헛돈을 날리다'. Compared with '돈 낭비', it carries a stronger feeling of regret.

examples.ko: 바퀴가 진흙에서 헛돌아서 차가 안 움직여요.
examples.en: The wheels spin in the mud, so the car won't move.
The screw just spins, so it won't tighten.
The tires spin in place on the snowy road.
The bicycle pedal spins freely and the chain has come off too.

examples.ko: 병뚜껑이 계속 헛돌아서 열 수가 없어요.
examples.en: The bottle cap keeps spinning, so I can't open it.

examples.ko: 열심히 하는데 요즘은 일이 헛도는 느낌이에요.
examples.en: I'm working hard, but lately it feels like I'm just spinning my wheels.

explain: 바퀴, 나사, 뚜껑처럼 돌기만 하고 물리지 않아서 앞으로 나가지 않을 때 써요. 사람이 애는 쓰는데 결과가 없을 때 비유로도 써요. 비슷한 '겉돌다'는 어울리지 못하고 따로 논다는 뜻이라 달라요.
explain_en: Use it when a wheel, screw, or cap turns but doesn't grip, so nothing moves forward. It can also be used figuratively for someone who tries hard with no result. '겉돌다' is different: it means not blending in and staying on the outside.

examples.en: What nonsense are you talking?
Everything that person says is nonsense.
Stop talking nonsense and just tell me the facts.
I had a high fever and talked deliriously all night.

examples.ko: 그런 소문을 믿다니, 그건 헛소리에 불과해요.
examples.en: How can you believe that rumor? It's nothing but nonsense.
My friend laughed and said I was talking nonsense again.

explain: 말투가 꽤 거칠어서 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요. 친한 사이에서는 '말도 안 되는 소리'를 가볍게 놀릴 때도 써요. 열이 심할 때 정신없이 하는 말도 '헛소리'라고 해요.
explain_en: The tone is rough, so avoid it with elders or people you've just met. Among close friends it can be a light tease for 'that makes no sense'. It also describes the incoherent talk of someone with a high fever.

en: be tangled; be entangled; be disheveled

examples.en: My hair got all messed up because of the wind.
My hair is always messy when I wake up.
The thread is so tangled that I can't undo it.

examples.ko: 헝클어진 머리로 학교에 갈 수는 없어요.
examples.en: I can't go to school with messy hair.

examples.ko: 방 안이 헝클어져 있어서 정리해야 해요.
examples.en: The room is a mess, so I need to tidy it up.

examples.ko: 서류가 헝클어지지 않게 파일에 꽂아 주세요.
examples.en: Please put the documents in a file so they don't get jumbled.

explain: 머리카락, 실, 끈처럼 길고 가는 것이 엉킬 때 가장 잘 어울려요. '흐트러지다'는 정돈된 것이 흩어질 때 쓰는 말이라 느낌이 조금 달라요. 사람이 일부러 그렇게 만들 때는 '머리를 헝클다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It fits best for long, thin things like hair, thread, or string that get tangled. '흐트러지다' is for something neat that scatters, so the feel is a little different. When a person does it on purpose, use the active verb, as in '머리를 헝클다'.

examples.en: I drive with the headlights on at night.
The oncoming car's headlights are too bright.
One headlight is out, so I need to get it repaired.
Turn on your headlights before entering the tunnel.

examples.ko: 안개가 짙은 날에는 헤드라이트를 켜야 안전해요.
examples.en: On very foggy days, it's safer to turn on the headlights.
The light of headlights approached from far away.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '헤드라이트'를 많이 쓰고, 설명서나 뉴스에서는 같은 뜻의 '전조등'도 자주 나와요. 차 뒤쪽의 등은 '후미등'이라고 해요. '켜다'와 '끄다'를 같이 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk people often say '헤드라이트', while manuals and news also use the equivalent '전조등'. The lights at the back of a car are '후미등'. It is used with the verbs '켜다' (turn on) and '끄다' (turn off).

examples.ko: 살이 빠져서 혁대 구멍을 한 칸 줄였어요.
examples.en: I lost weight, so I moved the belt in by one hole.
My pants kept slipping down, so I tightened my belt.
I bought a belt as a birthday present for my father.

examples.ko: 혁대 버클이 망가져서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: The belt buckle is broken, so I have to buy a new one.

examples.ko: 공항 검색대에서 혁대를 풀어 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: At airport security they asked me to take off my belt.

examples.ko: 혁대 없이도 입을 수 있는 바지예요.
examples.en: These are pants you can wear even without a belt.

explain: 요즘 일상 대화에서는 외래어인 '벨트'를 더 많이 쓰고, '혁대'는 조금 예스러운 느낌이 있어요. '허리띠'는 가죽이 아니어도 허리에 매는 띠를 두루 가리켜요. '혁대를 매다', '혁대를 풀다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: In everyday talk the loanword '벨트' is more common, and '혁대' sounds a bit old-fashioned. '허리띠' covers any band worn around the waist, not only leather. You say '혁대를 매다' (put on) and '혁대를 풀다' (take off).

examples.en: The skill gap between the two teams is huge.

examples.ko: 도시와 시골의 소득 격차가 현격하게 벌어졌어요.
examples.en: The income gap between city and countryside has widened considerably.
Our goal is to reduce the large difference.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 기술 수준은 그렇게 현격하지 않아요.
examples.en: The technology levels of the two countries are not that far apart.
The temperature people felt differed greatly from person to person.

examples.ko: 결과가 현격하게 달라서 다시 확인해 봤어요.
examples.en: The results were so different that I checked again.

explain: '차이', '격차', '간격' 같은 말 앞에서 자주 나와요. 둘을 비교해서 많이 다르다고 할 때 쓰는 글말 느낌의 표현이에요. 말할 때는 '차이가 엄청나요'처럼 더 쉽게 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It often appears before words like '차이', '격차', and '간격'. It is a somewhat written-style word used when comparing two things that differ a lot. In speech people often say something simpler like '차이가 엄청나요'.

examples.ko: 고전 소설을 현대어로 옮긴 책을 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a book that put a classic novel into modern language.
Please explain this poem in modern language.
Old speech is very different from modern language.
It's easy to understand once it is translated into modern language.

examples.ko: 국어 시간에 훈민정음을 현대어로 바꿔 봤어요.
examples.en: In Korean class, we turned Hunminjeongeum into modern language.

examples.ko: 현대어에서는 이 단어를 거의 안 써요.
examples.en: This word is hardly used in modern language.

explain: 주로 옛글이나 옛말과 비교할 때 쓰는 말이에요. '고어'나 '옛말'과 짝이 돼요. 고전을 읽을 때 '현대어 풀이'가 붙어 있는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is mostly used when contrasting with old writing or old speech, and pairs with '고어' and '옛말'. When you read classics, a '현대어 풀이' (modern-language explanation) is often attached.

examples.en: Modernizing the factory cost a lot of money.
The market modernization project will end soon.
Modernizing the hospital facilities is urgent.
Thanks to agricultural modernization, farming has become much easier.

examples.ko: 도시가 현대화되면서 옛 건물이 많이 사라졌어요.
examples.en: As the city modernized, many old buildings disappeared.
The hanok was modernized and turned into a cafe.

explain: 낡은 시설이나 제도를 새롭게 바꾼다는 뜻으로 '시설 현대화', '시장 현대화'처럼 자주 써요. '근대화'는 역사 이야기에서 더 많이 나와요. 동사로는 '현대화하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is often used in phrases like '시설 현대화' and '시장 현대화' for updating old facilities or systems. '근대화' appears more in historical contexts. The verb form is '현대화하다'.

examples.ko: 낡은 공장을 현대화하는 데 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes time to modernize the old factory.
They modernized the market, and customers increased.
City Hall decided to modernize the old library.
Clothes that modernize traditional hanbok are popular.
They modernized the school cafeteria this year.
If we don't modernize the equipment, it's hard to compete.

explain: 시설, 제도, 설비를 새것처럼 바꿀 때 써요. 전통 옷을 요즘 스타일로 바꾼 것은 '개량 한복'이라고도 해요. 받는 쪽을 주어로 하고 싶으면 '현대화되다'를 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: Use it when making facilities, systems, or equipment up to date. A traditional outfit adapted to modern style is also called '개량 한복'. If you want the thing being modernized as the subject, you can use '현대화되다'.

examples.ko: 정부가 임금을 물가에 맞게 현실화하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The government decided to adjust wages realistically to match prices.

examples.ko: 오랜 꿈을 현실화하기 위해 열심히 준비해요.
examples.en: I'm preparing hard to make my long-held dream a reality.
The thing I was worried about has come true, so I feel heavy-hearted.
They demanded that the compensation be set at a realistic level.
To make the plan real, we need money.
The people who turn ideas into reality are the ones who succeed.

explain: 두 가지로 써요. 꿈이나 걱정이 실제로 일어나게 만든다는 뜻, 그리고 요금이나 임금을 현실에 맞게 조정한다는 뜻이에요. 뉴스에서는 '요금 현실화'처럼 많이 나오고, 일상에서는 '이루다'를 더 자주 써요. 걱정이 실제로 일어날 때는 '현실화되다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It has two uses: making a dream or worry actually happen, and adjusting fees or wages to match reality. In news you often see '요금 현실화', while in daily talk '이루다' is more common for dreams. When a worry actually happens, people say '현실화되다'.

examples.en: I have worked on the front lines for ten years.
I listened to a teacher who is working in the field.

examples.ko: 현업 종사자들은 이 제도가 불편하다고 해요.
examples.en: People working in the field say this system is inconvenient.
After being promoted, I left the front line and became a manager.

examples.ko: 현업 경험이 있는 사람을 뽑고 싶어요.
examples.en: We want to hire someone with hands-on work experience.

examples.ko: 학교에서 배우는 내용은 현업과 많이 달라요.
examples.en: What you learn at school is quite different from real work.

explain: 사무나 관리보다는 실제 일이 벌어지는 자리에서 하는 업무를 가리켜요. '현업 부서', '현업 종사자'처럼 자주 써요. 회사 이야기에서 많이 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: It points to work done where things actually happen, as opposed to office or management work. It is common in phrases like '현업 부서' and '현업 종사자'. You hear it mostly in talk about companies.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 현장감이 넘쳐서 실제 같아요.
examples.en: This movie is so vivid that it feels real.
You can feel the atmosphere just by looking at the photo.
The reporter described the situation vividly, as if on the spot.

examples.ko: 극장에서 보면 소리 때문에 현장감이 더 좋아요.
examples.en: In a theater, the sound makes it feel even more real.
The story felt so real that I listened closely.

examples.ko: 이 글은 현장감이 부족해서 읽기 지루해요.
examples.en: This text lacks vividness, so it's boring to read.

explain: '현장감이 있다', '현장감이 넘치다', '현장감이 살아 있다'처럼 칭찬할 때 자주 써요. 사진, 영상, 소리, 글이 마치 그 자리에 있는 것 같을 때 어울려요. '생생하다'와 같이 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is often used as praise, as in '현장감이 있다', '현장감이 넘치다', and '현장감이 살아 있다'. It fits photos, video, sound, or writing that makes you feel you are right there. It also goes well with '생생하다' (vivid).

examples.en: Please write your current address accurately on the form.

examples.ko: 이 책은 한국 교육의 현주소를 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This book shows the current state of Korean education.
This is the current state of our society.

examples.ko: 현주소를 알아야 앞으로 계획을 세울 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to know where you stand now to make plans.
I checked where my skills stand now with a mock exam.

examples.ko: 이 기사는 청년 취업의 현주소를 다뤄요.
examples.en: This article covers the current situation of youth employment.

explain: 서류에서는 지금 살고 있는 주소를 뜻하고, 옛 주소나 본적과 구분할 때 써요. 일상에서는 오히려 '~의 현주소'처럼 지금의 상태나 수준을 말하는 비유로 더 많이 나와요. 말로 집 주소를 물을 때는 그냥 '주소'라고 해요.

phrases.en: This statistic is the current state of youth unemployment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일의 지금 모습이나 수준을 그대로 보여 줄 때 써요. 주로 뉴스나 글에서 나오고, 좋지 않은 현실을 말할 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to show the present state or level of something as it really is. It appears mostly in news and writing, often about an unfavorable reality.

explain_en: On forms it means the address where you live now, as distinct from an old address or registered domicile. In daily use it appears more often figuratively, as '~의 현주소', meaning the current state or level of something. When asking for a home address in speech, people just say '주소'.

examples.en: At the hospital, they measured my blood pressure with a monitor.
I bought a blood pressure monitor to use at home.
The numbers look strange, so the monitor may be broken.

examples.ko: 약국에 가면 혈압계가 있어서 무료로 잴 수 있어요.
examples.en: There is a blood pressure monitor at the pharmacy, so you can measure for free.

examples.ko: 할머니는 매일 아침 혈압계를 팔에 감아요.
examples.en: Grandmother wraps the blood pressure cuff around her arm every morning.

examples.ko: 손목에 차는 혈압계는 편하지만 덜 정확하대요.
examples.en: I heard wrist monitors are convenient but less accurate.

explain: '체온계', '온도계'처럼 재는 기계 이름에는 '-계'가 붙어요. 혈압은 '혈압을 재다'로 말하고, 재는 기계는 '혈압계'라고 해요. 팔에 감는 팔뚝형과 손목에 차는 손목형이 있고, 손목형은 팔뚝형보다 덜 정확하다고들 해요.
explain_en: Like '체온계' and '온도계', names of measuring devices take '-계'. You say '혈압을 재다' for taking blood pressure, and '혈압계' for the device. There are arm-cuff and wrist types, and wrist types are often said to be less accurate than arm-cuff ones.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 혈연관계가 아니지만 친형제처럼 지내요.
examples.en: They aren't blood relatives, but they live like real brothers.
I heard they took a DNA test to confirm the blood relation.

examples.ko: 혈연관계가 없어도 가족이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can become a family even without blood ties.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 대부분 혈연관계로 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: Most people in this village are connected by blood ties.

examples.ko: 회사에서 혈연관계로 사람을 뽑으면 공정하지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't fair if a company hires people because of family ties.

examples.ko: 혈연관계보다 오래 함께 산 정이 더 중요할 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes the bond from living together long matters more than blood relation.

explain: '혈연'은 피로 이어진 사이이고, '혈연관계'는 그 관계를 말해요. 같은 고향 사람끼리의 '지연', 같은 학교 출신끼리의 '학연'과 함께 '혈연·지연·학연'으로 묶어 말하는 경우가 많아요. 순우리말로는 '핏줄'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '혈연' is a tie by blood, and '혈연관계' is that relationship. It is often grouped as '혈연·지연·학연' with '지연' (ties from the same hometown) and '학연' (ties from the same school). The native Korean word is '핏줄'.

examples.en: Our class has a good cooperative atmosphere.
A cooperative attitude is the key to the team's success.

examples.ko: 협동적 학습 방법이 아이들에게 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Collaborative learning methods help children.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 협동적 성격이라서 같이 일하기 편해요.
examples.en: That friend is cooperative by nature, so he's easy to work with.
At daycare, children do a lot of cooperative play.

examples.ko: 협동적 관계를 만들려면 서로 양보해야 해요.
examples.en: To build a cooperative relationship, you have to give way to each other.

explain: '-적'이 붙은 말이라 뒤에 명사가 오는 '협동적 태도'도 쓰고, '협동적인 태도'처럼 '인'을 붙여서도 자주 말해요. 서술할 때는 '협동적이다'로 써요. 반대로 서로 이기려는 모습은 '경쟁적'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Because it ends in '-적', you can say '협동적 태도' before a noun, and also '협동적인 태도' with '인', which is very common. To describe someone, use '협동적이다'. The opposite, where people try to beat each other, is '경쟁적'.

examples.en: I must have been tired, because sores came up on my tongue.

examples.ko: 혓바늘 때문에 밥 먹을 때 아파요.
examples.en: Because of the tongue sores, it hurts when I eat.

examples.ko: 혓바늘이 나서 매운 음식을 못 먹겠어요.
examples.en: I have a sore tongue, so I can't eat spicy food.

examples.ko: 요즘 잠을 못 자서 혓바늘이 자꾸 생겨요.
examples.en: I'm not sleeping well lately, so tongue sores keep appearing.
Tongue sores usually go away after a few days.
They say that when tongue sores pop up, it's a sign your body is tired.

explain: 혀 위에 바늘처럼 작게 솟는 붉은 것이에요. '혓바늘이 돋다', '혓바늘이 나다', '혓바늘이 생기다'라고 써요. 피곤할 때 생긴다고 많이들 말해요.
explain_en: These are small, needle-like red bumps that rise on the tongue. You say '혓바늘이 돋다', '혓바늘이 나다', or '혓바늘이 생기다'. Many people say they appear when you are tired.

examples.en: I burned my tongue on the hot soup.
The child stuck out his tongue and laughed.
The puppy licked my hand with its tongue.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 혓바닥만 길고 행동은 안 해요.
examples.en: That person is all talk and doesn't take action.
After eating the candy, my tongue turned blue.
The doctor told me to stick out my tongue.

explain: '혀'보다 속되고 거친 느낌이 있어서, 격식 있는 자리나 병원 설명에서는 '혀'를 써요. 귀엽게 말하거나 친구끼리 편하게 말할 때, 또는 말만 앞서는 사람을 낮춰 말할 때 나와요. 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It sounds cruder than '혀', so in formal situations or medical explanations people use '혀'. It shows up in casual talk among friends, when speaking playfully, or when putting down someone who is all talk. Avoid it with elders.

examples.en: Brothers should live helping each other.
Even though we're brothers, our personalities are completely different.

examples.ko: 형제지간이라도 돈 문제는 분명히 해야 해요.
examples.en: Even between brothers, money matters should be made clear.
The two of them are as close as brothers.
If siblings fight often, their parents get upset.

examples.ko: 저 형제지간이 얼마나 사이가 좋은지 부러워요.
examples.en: I envy how well those two brothers get along.

explain: '형제 사이'라는 뜻의 말이에요. 비슷한 말로 '형제간', '남매지간', '자매지간'이 있어요. 실제 형제가 아니어도 '형제지간처럼 친하다'고 비유해서 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means the relationship between brothers. Similar words are '형제간', '남매지간', and '자매지간'. Even for people who aren't actual brothers, you can say they are '형제지간처럼' close, as a comparison.

examples.en: I did terribly on the exam, so I'm upset.

examples.ko: 어제 경기에서 우리 팀이 형편없이 졌어요.
examples.en: Our team lost badly in yesterday's game.
My cooking skills are awfully clumsy.
The service at that restaurant was terribly bad.
I got rained on, and my clothes got completely soaked.
I went to karaoke after a long time and sang terribly.

explain: '형편없다'의 부사형으로, 뒤에 '지다', '나쁘다', '서툴다'처럼 좋지 않은 말이 자주 와요. '엉망으로'와 비슷하지만 수준이 매우 낮다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 명사 앞에서는 '형편없는'을 써요.
explain_en: This is the adverb form of '형편없다', and it is often followed by negative words like '지다' (lose), '나쁘다', and '서툴다'. It resembles '엉망으로' (in a mess), but feels more like the level is extremely low. Before a noun, use '형편없는'.

examples.ko: 정원에서 호랑나비 한 마리가 꽃에 앉았어요.
examples.en: A swallowtail butterfly landed on a flower in the garden.
The wings of a swallowtail have yellow patterns.

examples.ko: 호랑나비 애벌레를 키워 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever raised swallowtail caterpillars?
When spring came, swallowtail butterflies began flying around.
The child ran to catch a swallowtail butterfly.
I took a photo of a swallowtail with beautiful patterns.

explain: 날개의 줄무늬가 호랑이 무늬 같다고 해서 붙은 이름으로 알려져 있어요. 흰나비, 노랑나비처럼 색 이름이 붙은 나비와는 달리 큰 무늬가 특징이에요.
explain_en: It is known as the 'tiger' butterfly because its wing stripes look like a tiger's. Unlike butterflies named for a color, such as '흰나비' and '노랑나비', it stands out for its bold patterns.

examples.en: The police officer blew a whistle and stopped the car.

examples.ko: 체육 선생님이 호루라기를 불자 모두 모였어요.
examples.en: When the gym teacher blew the whistle, everyone gathered.
I was startled by the sound of a whistle.

examples.ko: 등산할 때 위급하면 호루라기를 불어서 알려요.
examples.en: When hiking, if there's an emergency, blow a whistle to signal.

examples.ko: 목에 호루라기를 걸고 있는 사람이 심판이에요.
examples.en: The person with a whistle around his neck is the referee.

examples.ko: 호루라기가 고장 났는지 소리가 안 나요.
examples.en: It doesn't make a sound, so the whistle may be broken.

explain: 도구로 부는 '호루라기'는 '불다'와 함께 써요. 입술로 내는 소리는 '휘파람'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 심판, 경찰, 선생님이 신호를 줄 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The device '호루라기' goes with the verb '불다' (blow). A whistle made with your lips is '휘파람', which is different. It often appears with referees, police, and teachers giving signals.

examples.en: That actor is tall and slender.

examples.ko: 동생은 호리호리한 체격이라 옷이 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: My younger brother is slim, so clothes look good on him.
He looks slim, but he's strong.
I exercise every day to keep a slender figure.
He is a slender young man with a fair face.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 호리호리했는데 지금은 많이 쪘어요.
examples.en: I was slim as a kid, but I've put on a lot of weight now.

explain: 키가 크면서 몸이 가늘고 날렵한 모습에 어울려요. '날씬하다'가 살이 적고 보기 좋다는 느낌이라면, '호리호리하다'는 길쭉하고 가는 몸매를 그려요. '마르다'는 때때로 걱정스러운 느낌이 있어서 말투가 달라요.
explain_en: It suits a body that is tall, thin, and lithe. '날씬하다' feels like being slim in a nice way, while '호리호리하다' paints a long, slender build. '마르다' can sound worrisome, so the tone is different.

examples.en: Yellow pumpkin flowers bloomed in the yard.
A bee flew in and landed on the pumpkin flower.
Grandmother made pan-fried pancakes with pumpkin flowers for me.
On the summer morning the pumpkin flowers opened wide.
I went to the vegetable garden to take photos of pumpkin flowers.
Pumpkin flowers are big and have a vivid color.

explain: 호박 덩굴에 피는 노란 꽃이에요. 시골 텃밭이나 집 마당에서 흔히 볼 수 있어요. 꽃을 음식 재료로 쓰는 집도 있어요.
explain_en: It is the yellow flower that blooms on pumpkin vines. You often see it in country vegetable gardens and yards. Some households also use the flowers as a food ingredient.

examples.en: You peel the shell of pumpkin seeds before eating them.
I roasted pumpkin seeds and ate them as a snack.
I heard pumpkin seeds have many nutrients that are good for the body.
Grandmother dried the pumpkin seeds and set them aside.
I sprinkled pumpkin seeds on top of the salad.

examples.ko: 호박씨 껍질을 까는 데 손이 많이 가요.
examples.en: Peeling pumpkin seeds takes a lot of effort.

explain: 볶아서 간식이나 안주로, 또 샐러드나 죽에 넣어 먹어요. 껍질을 까서 먹는 씨앗이라 '호박씨를 까다'라고 해요. 이 '까다'가 아래 관용 표현에도 쓰여요.

phrases.example: 얌전한 줄 알았는데 뒤에서 호박씨를 깠어요.
phrases.en: I thought he was quiet, but he was up to something behind my back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로는 얌전하고 아무것도 모르는 척하면서 뒤에서 몰래 딴짓을 하거나 제 이익을 챙길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone acts quiet and innocent on the surface but secretly does something else or looks after their own interests behind the scenes.
phrases.en_equiv: do something sneaky behind one's back

explain_en: They are roasted and eaten as a snack, or added to salads and porridge. Since you peel the shell, the verb is '호박씨를 까다'. That same '까다' is used in the idiom below.

examples.ko: 암 환자들이 호스피스 병동에서 편안하게 지내요.
examples.en: Cancer patients stay comfortably in the hospice ward.
My mother spent her final days in a hospice.
I applied for hospice volunteer work.
Hospice care focuses on comfort rather than treatment.
The family is looking into hospice hospitals.
A hospice nurse takes care of the patient and the family.

explain: 일반 병원이 병을 고치는 데 목표를 두는 것과 달리, 통증을 줄이고 환자와 가족의 마음을 돌보는 데 중심을 둬요. 법과 뉴스에서는 '호스피스·완화의료'를 함께 말하는 경우가 많아요. 장소를 말할 때는 '호스피스 병동'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Unlike a regular hospital that aims to cure illness, it focuses on easing pain and caring for the patient and family emotionally. In law and news, 'hospice and palliative care' (호스피스·완화의료) are often mentioned together. For the place, people say '호스피스 병동'.

examples.en: Father yelled at my older brother who came home late.
The teacher bellowed at the students who were making noise.
An angry customer is yelling at the staff member.

examples.ko: 큰 소리로 호통치지 않아도 아이는 알아들어요.
examples.en: A child understands even if you don't bellow at them.

examples.ko: 사장님이 크게 호통치는 바람에 모두 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The boss roared so loudly that everyone was startled.
Grandmother may yell, but she soon laughs again.

explain: 주로 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 화가 나서 크게 소리를 지르며 꾸짖을 때 써요. '꾸짖다'보다 목소리가 크고 기세가 센 느낌이에요. '호통을 치다'로 띄어 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used when someone in a higher position scolds a person below them in a loud, angry voice. It feels louder and more forceful than '꾸짖다'. You will also see it written as '호통을 치다'.

examples.en: The patient fell into a coma after a car accident.
He woke up from the coma after a week.
When a coma drags on, the family has a hard time.

examples.ko: 환자가 혼수상태라서 말을 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The patient is in a coma, so he can't speak.

examples.ko: 의사가 혼수상태인 환자를 계속 살펴보고 있어요.
examples.en: The doctor keeps watching the patient who is in a coma.

examples.ko: 갑자기 쓰러진 할아버지가 혼수상태로 병원에 실려 왔어요.
examples.en: Grandfather suddenly collapsed and was brought to the hospital in a coma.

explain: '혼수상태에 빠지다'와 '혼수상태에서 깨어나다'가 짝처럼 자주 나와요. 뉴스에서는 '의식 불명'이라는 표현도 많이 쓰는데, 병원 설명에서는 '혼수상태'가 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '혼수상태에 빠지다' (fall into a coma) and '혼수상태에서 깨어나다' (wake from a coma) often appear as a pair. News also uses '의식 불명' (unconscious), while '혼수상태' is more common in medical explanations.

en: wedding furnishings; items prepared for marriage

examples.ko: 결혼 전에 혼수품을 사러 가구점에 갔어요.
examples.en: Before the wedding, I went to a furniture store to buy items for the new home.

examples.ko: 혼수품 때문에 두 집안이 의견이 달랐어요.
examples.en: The two families disagreed over the wedding household items.
The bride's mother wrote down a list of wedding items.

examples.ko: 요즘은 혼수품을 간단하게 준비하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: These days many people prepare wedding household items simply.
We bought a refrigerator and a washing machine as wedding household items.

examples.ko: 혼수품은 신혼집에 맞춰서 고르는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to choose wedding household items to fit the newlyweds' home.

explain: 결혼할 때 새 살림을 위해 마련하는 가구, 가전, 옷, 이불 같은 물건을 말해요. 줄여서 '혼수'라고도 하고, '혼수를 준비하다', '혼수를 해 가다'처럼 써요. 결혼 이야기에서 가끔 부담스러운 주제로 나오기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to furniture, appliances, clothes, bedding, and other things prepared for a new household at marriage. It is often shortened to '혼수', as in '혼수를 준비하다'. In talk about weddings it can sometimes be a touchy topic because of the cost.

examples.ko: 월급을 하루 만에 홀라당 써 버렸어요.
examples.en: I spent my whole paycheck in just one day.
The wind blew, and my hat flew right off.
My younger sibling ate up the whole cake.

examples.ko: 불이 나서 집이 홀라당 타 버렸어요.
examples.en: A fire broke out, and the house burned down completely.
I got scammed and lost all my money.

examples.ko: 방금 널었는데 빨래가 비에 홀라당 젖었어요.
examples.en: I had just hung out the laundry, and it got totally soaked by the rain.

explain: 어떤 것이 순식간에 몽땅 없어지거나 완전히 달라질 때 쓰는 가벼운 구어체예요. '-아/어 버리다'와 함께 자주 나오고, 아쉬운 일에 많이 써요. '홀딱'과 비슷한 느낌으로 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: A light, colloquial word for something disappearing entirely in an instant or changing completely. It often appears with '-아/어 버리다', usually for regrettable things. It can feel similar to '홀딱'.

examples.en: I grew up under my single mother.
He lives with and takes care of his widowed mother.
A single mother raised three children by herself.
He is the only son of a widowed mother, so he is very devoted.

examples.ko: 홀어머니를 위해 작은 집을 한 채 마련했어요.
examples.en: I got a small house for my widowed mother.
The single mother runs the shop all by herself.

explain: 남편 없이 혼자 지내거나 아이를 키우는 어머니를 말하고, 아버지 쪽은 '홀아버지'예요. 요즘 일상에서는 '한부모 가정'처럼 중립적인 표현을 쓰는 경우가 많아요. '홀어머니 밑에서 자라다'라는 말이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to a mother who lives alone or raises children without a husband, and the father's counterpart is '홀아버지'. These days a neutral expression like '한부모 가정' (single-parent family) is often used in daily talk. The phrase '홀어머니 밑에서 자라다' (grow up with a single mother) is common.
